findings.title: Zero/negative inner vector dimensions let one payload byte drive a huge slice allocation
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize floors any inner vector with Dimensions <= 0 to 1 byte, and the parser (frame.go:861, dim, _ := strconv.Atoi(...)) still accepts such dimensions since the dim < 1 rejection said to land with #1093 isn't present. For vector<vector<float,-3>,M> or vector<vector<float,0>,M> with an L-byte payload, the guard accepts M = L, so reflect.MakeSlice allocates about 24*L bytes before the inner decoder errors (about 12 B per payload byte for vector<vector<text,1>,N>), contradicting the PR's flat 3.5 KB claim. The same cause also wrongly rejects a valid empty vector<vector<float,0>,M> payload that actually encodes in 0 bytes.

findings.title: 32-bit wrap-arithmetic coverage claim can never run since the package doesn't build on 386
findings.claim: The wrap arithmetic is correct in principle (bits.UintSize gives 1<<29+1, which wraps to 8 on 386), but GOARCH=386 go vet . exits 1 because dependencies don't compile, e.g. serialization/varint/unmarshal_ints.go:25 and serialization/cqlint/unmarshal_utils.go:13 overflow. So the package does not build on 386 and these tests can never run there.

findings.title: Comment claims no element describes zero bytes, but vector<float,0> is exactly zero bytes
findings.claim: The comment says 'Neither can describe an element in zero bytes', but vector<float,0> is exactly zero bytes; the 1 is only a divide-by-zero clamp.

findings.title: Comment claims an N-element vector is never fewer than N bytes, broken by zero-dim…
findings.claim: The comment states 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes', which vector<vector<float,0>,N> breaks by encoding in 0 bytes.

findings.title: Comment conflates one inner vector's byte size with the whole fixture's size
findings.claim: The comment says 'Each inner vector … eight bytes', but each inner vector<text,3> is actually 1+3=4 bytes; 8 is the size of the two-element payload checked at :780.

findings.title: Stale comment claims nil/empty and dim=0 still fall through to the generic path
findings.claim: The comment 'nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path' no longer holds: with dim > 0, an empty non-nil payload is now rejected at :1000, and negative dimensions error at :992.

findings.title: Comment overclaims that every path below turns the payload into an allocation
findings.claim: The claim 'every path below turns it into an allocation' is false for array destinations, which only compare lengths rather than allocate.

findings.title: Nested vector type errors omit the inner element type and dimension
findings.claim: VectorType has no String(), and a nested type parsed from the wire keeps only the bare ...VectorType prefix (helpers.go:271), so the new error renders as custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType) with no element type or dimension. Likewise the bound error at :1001 doesn't give elemMin, so it can't show why a nested count was rejected, and the subtest at :872 only matches the generic string 'no Go type for element type'.

findings.title: Duplicate condition info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil appears in two separate blocks
findings.claim: Both the block at :998 and :1007 test the same condition info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil; the bound could open the fast-path block instead, which would also make the 'multiplication is safe' ordering obvious.

findings.title: Commits and PR body carry Claude/Anthropic attribution against user rule
findings.claim: Commits 0276a66 and 78891dd both carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>', and the PR body ends with '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]', both forbidden by the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: PR body's referenced issue numbers don't resolve in the repo
findings.claim: gh issue view finds none of #1085, #1086, #1106, #1093 or #1091 in dkropachev/tidepool, so the PR body's out-of-scope and 'lands with' claims point at nothing.

findings.title: Commit 0276a66's body describes the design it replaced, not what it adds
findings.claim: The commit body says 'Every element takes at least one byte on the wire', but the commit itself adds the recursive vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1125), and the test comment at :831 explains that a one-byte floor is not enough.

findings.title: Commit 78891dd's subject omits a wider behavioral change it includes
findings.claim: The subject covers only the vector guard, but the helpers.go:282 change makes every unknown type name, from every caller (collections, UDTs, tuples, frame.go), keep its name in Custom()/String(); it is tested only through the vector error path.

findings.title: Three element-size classifiers must be kept manually in sync
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize, vectorFixedElemSize and isVectorVariableLengthType all classify the same element types; a type added to one but not the others would silently shift the bound. A cross-check test or a doc line naming the dependency would help.

findings.title: Nested vector size classification cost grows quadratically with nesting depth
findings.claim: Each level calls isVectorVariableLengthType, which walks the remaining depth again, so cost grows with nesting depth squared; the server controls depth through the type string, though the cost is bounded by that string's length.

findings.title: makeVectorType duplicates makeDoubleVectorType with arguments that can disagree
findings.claim: makeVectorType repeats the existing makeDoubleVectorType (:35), and its separate elem and elemName arguments can disagree with each other.

findings.title: makeNestedVectorType builds a custom name that differs from what the parser actually…
findings.claim: makeNestedVectorType builds a custom name that differs from the bare ...VectorType prefix the parser actually produces.

findings.title: wireVectorType helper name doesn't convey that it parses via framer.readTypeInfo
findings.claim: wireVectorType actually parses through framer.readTypeInfo; a name that says so would be clearer.

findings.title: New tests use t.Parallel() while the file's existing tests don't
findings.claim: New tests use t.Parallel(); the file's existing tests don't, which is inconsistent within the file though not wrong.

findings.title: Allocation test reads process-wide TotalAlloc, which stray goroutines could make noisy
findings.claim: The allocation test reads process-wide TotalAlloc, so stray background goroutines can add noise; the 128 KiB threshold leaves wide margin, and the '25 MB' figure is correct on 64-bit (2^20 x 24 B).

findings.title: Comment confirmed still accurate
findings.claim: The comment at marshal.go:978 is still accurate.

findings.title: "// basic type" comment now also covers the fallback to a named custom type
findings.claim: The '// basic type' comment at helpers.go:279 now also covers the fallback to a named custom type.

findings.title: PR body's claim that every new test fails against pristine code overstates the reason
findings.claim: This is true only because the base fails to compile without vectorElemMinSize; on behavior alone, TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads would pass on base.

findings.title: "Short or zero-length payload now errors" claim applies only to fixed-size elements
findings.claim: This applies only to fixed-size elements; variable-length elements already errored on empty data at base, and three empty texts (3 bytes) still decode.
